articles.title: Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium in adolescent athletes with acute groin pain: clinical and MRI features of a radiograph-occult injury pattern.
articles.authors: Sakoda S, Kajiwara K, Nagaoka R, Kawano K
articles.population: Athletes aged 22 years or under with acute sports-related groin pain and negative or inconclusive radiographs
articles.sample_size: 20 of 91 patients (22.0%) met MRI criteria for subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium
articles.outcomes: Return to unrestricted sports participation after progressive rehabilitation; mean time 4.5 weeks. Associated anterior inferior iliac spine avulsion or iliacus injury in 50% of patients. All managed nonoperatively.
articles.take_home: Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium is an injury to young athletes' hip bones that does not show up on standard X-rays but can be seen on MRI scans. Young athletes with this injury recovered well with nonsurgical treatment and returned to full sports in about 4 and a half weeks on average.

articles.title: Preoperative ultrasound in pediatric supracondylar fracture-related nerve injuries: intraoperative correlation in a tertiary referral retrospective case series.
articles.authors: Abukar A, Alfonso Palanca P, Yogarajah N, Sugand K, Pressney I, Panagiotidou A, et al.
articles.population: Children under 16 years with persistent nerve palsy after supracondylar humeral fracture
articles.outcomes: Ultrasound detection of nerve abnormality and concordance with intraoperative findings
articles.take_home: Ultrasound successfully detected nerve problems in 95% of children with persistent nerve injury after supracondylar fractures, but it was not always accurate at identifying the specific type of nerve problem compared to what surgeons found during operation. Ultrasound should be used alongside clinical assessment rather than on its own to decide whether surgery is needed.

articles.title: Trisomy 21 and Patellar Femoral Instability in a Pediatric Population: Results From 53,800 Patients.
articles.authors: Magoline JA, Yoder RG, Morscher MA, Riley PM Jr, Bono KT, Polousky JD, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis using electronic health records
articles.population: Children with Trisomy 21 aged 19 years or younger, compared with age, sex, race and ethnicity-matched children without Trisomy 21
articles.sample_size: 53,800 patients with Trisomy 21; 347 with patellofemoral instability matched with 347 non-Trisomy 21 patients
articles.outcomes: Annual prevalence of patellofemoral instability in Trisomy 21 patients; rates of surgical intervention; mean age at diagnosis; time from diagnosis to surgery
articles.take_home: Children with Trisomy 21 have lower rates of patellofemoral instability than previously thought, but are nearly twice as likely to need surgery for it compared with other children with the same condition. Girls with Trisomy 21 are more affected than boys.

articles.title: Long-term results of the modified Dunn procedure in slipped capital femoral epiphysis : a minimum of ten-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Aprato A, Audisio A, Grilli S, Giachino M, Reinaudo V, Risitano S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with stable or unstable slipped capital femoral epiphysis treated with modified Dunn procedure
articles.outcomes: Ten-year survival free from conversion to total hip replacement and radiological osteoarthritis progression; functional scores; hip range of motion; correction of femoral deformity angles
articles.take_home: The modified Dunn procedure achieved good long-term results with 88.6% of hips avoiding hip replacement at ten years and high functional scores. However, patients with severe slips had higher rates of osteoarthritis progression compared to those with mild or moderate slips.

articles.title: Osteochondral lesions of the talus in the pediatric population: A practical narrative review.
articles.authors: Turati M, Gatti SD, Thusing M, Guelfi M, Crippa M, Sinikumpu J, et al.
articles.population: Children and adolescents with osteochondral lesions of the talus
articles.outcomes: Assessment and treatment options including imaging modalities, nonoperative management, surgical techniques, and rehabilitation
articles.take_home: Osteochondral lesions of the talus in children can cause persistent ankle pain after injury and are best detected by MRI rather than plain X-rays. Treatment depends on whether the lesion is stable, ranging from conservative management for stable lesions to various surgical options including drilling, bone marrow stimulation, or fragment fixation for more complex cases.

articles.title: A modified Dunn osteotomy without surgical hip dislocation for severe slipped capital femoral epiphysis: mid-term outcomes from a case series.
articles.authors: Ouyang Z, Fu Z, Chen X, Wang L, Zhang Z, Liu T
articles.population: Children and young people with severe slipped capital femoral epiphysis
articles.outcomes: Slip angle, alpha angle, Tonnis grade, Harris Hip Score, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index, avascular necrosis, femoroacetabular impingement
articles.take_home: A modified hip operation without full hip dislocation successfully corrected severe slipped capital femoral epiphysis with good pain scores and no signs of osteoarthritis at an average follow-up of 4.7 years. The main risk was avascular necrosis in one patient with acute unstable disease, but avoiding full hip dislocation may help protect the blood supply to the hip bone.

articles.title: Temporary screw epiphysiodesis for correction of ankle valgus in children with multiple hereditary exostoses : a case-control study.
articles.authors: Schmitz SI, Broja M, Andresen A, Doerell A, Saegebrecht L, Rupprecht M, et al.
articles.population: Children with multiple hereditary exostoses (MHE) and idiopathic ankle valgus
articles.sample_size: 37 MHE patients (68 ankles) and 35 control patients (56 ankles)
articles.outcomes: Correction of ankle valgus measured by lateral distal tibia angle; correction rate per month; wearing time of the device; complications
articles.take_home: Temporary screw epiphysiodesis effectively corrects ankle valgus in children with MHE, but the correction happens more slowly than in children without MHE, meaning the surgery needs to be done earlier to achieve good results. Complications were rare, occurring in only 5 ankles.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life after calcaneus fractures in childhood and adolescence.
articles.authors: Milosevic M, Muller C, Bullmann T, Krause T, Ziebarth K
articles.population: Children and adolescents treated for calcaneus fractures
articles.outcomes: Health-related quality of life measured by Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM) and Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) at mean follow-up of 6.3 years
articles.take_home: Children and adolescents with heel bone fractures had excellent quality of life scores overall at follow-up of around 6 years. Those with the more serious joint depression type fractures had somewhat lower scores, but outcomes were still very good compared to what is seen in adults.

articles.title: Early functional and operative outcomes of three open surgical approaches compared with closed reduction and percutaneous pinning in Gartland type III pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures.
articles.authors: Karapinar SE, Kizilkaya V, Oguzlar FC, Hatip AY, Tunc A
articles.population: Children with Gartland type III supracondylar humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Operative time, fluoroscopy use, union time, joint range of motion, Flynn functional and cosmetic scores, complication rates
articles.take_home: Closed reduction and percutaneous pinning resulted in shorter surgery time, faster healing, and better cosmetic results than open surgery approaches. Among open surgery techniques, the anterior approach performed better than the posterior approach.

articles.title: Outcomes of greater trochanter-sparing proximal femoral resection as a hip salvage procedure in cerebral palsy patients.
articles.authors: Emet A, Armet G, Luck C, Aksoy T, Mendelson SA, Dede O
articles.population: Nonambulatory children with cerebral palsy (GMFCS IV-V) undergoing hip surgery
articles.outcomes: Radiographic migration, heterotopic ossification, hip range of motion, caregiver-reported functional improvement using Care and Comfort Caregiver Questionnaire
articles.take_home: Greater trochanter-sparing proximal femoral resection significantly improved caregiver satisfaction and comfort scores in children with severe cerebral palsy. Although the surgery caused some hip bone movement and abnormal bone formation, these changes did not affect the functional improvements reported by carers.

articles.title: Oral deucrictibant for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks: a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial.
articles.authors: Riedl MA, Li PH, Adatia A, Cancian M, Stobiecki M, Valerieva A, et al.
articles.study_type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial
articles.population: Adolescents and adults aged 12 to 75 years with hereditary angioedema
articles.sample_size: 134 participants randomised; 88 with paired treated attacks in primary efficacy analysis
articles.outcomes: Time to onset of symptom relief (primary endpoint); safety and adverse events
articles.take_home: Deucrictibant, an oral tablet taken on demand, reduced the time to symptom relief in hereditary angioedema attacks to about 1.3 hours compared with over 12 hours for placebo, with very few side effects reported.

articles.title: Modified radiographic classification for postaxial polydactyly of the foot: An analysis of 121 digits in 98 children.
articles.authors: Wu J, Li C, Luo X, Hua Z, Hu J, Li J, et al.
articles.population: Children with congenital postaxial polydactyly of the foot
articles.outcomes: Evaluation of imaging features and development of a modified radiographic classification system with assessment of reliability
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a new classification system for extra toes that is more comprehensive than existing systems and can classify almost all cases (97.5% compared to 89-93% with older systems). The new classification system showed excellent reliability for both individual and different raters, making it more useful for doctors to communicate about these cases and plan treatment.

articles.title: Guided growth for idiopathic genu valgum: analyzing the incidence and risk of rebound.
articles.authors: Kohan Fortuna Figueira S, Turazza F, Halliburton C, Colombo C, Allende V, Puigdevall M, et al.
articles.population: Paediatric patients with idiopathic genu valgum (knock knees) treated with tension-band plates
articles.outcomes: Incidence of rebound (return of the deformity) after implant removal; factors associated with rebound risk
articles.take_home: Two-thirds of children experienced some return of knock-knee after the correction plates were removed, but few needed further surgery. Faster correction during treatment was linked to a higher chance of rebound occurring afterwards.

articles.title: LongTerm Outcomes of Suspected Transient Synovitis of the Hip in NonAspirated Patients.
articles.authors: Smadi Z, Burnett J, Varghese J, Balaji S, Rosenfeld S
articles.population: Children diagnosed with transient synovitis of the hip managed without aspiration
articles.outcomes: Residual symptoms, recurrence of synovitis, rheumatologic or sequelae diagnoses, and missed diagnoses of septic arthritis assessed at 4 weeks, 6 months, 1 year, and 5 years
articles.take_home: Children with suspected transient synovitis managed without hip aspiration had very good long-term outcomes with no missed cases of septic arthritis. However, a small number of patients (3.2%) later developed rheumatologic conditions like juvenile idiopathic arthritis, so continued follow-up is important if symptoms persist or recur.

articles.title: Missing the Deadline: Predictors of Surgical Delay Beyond 18 Hours in Pediatric Supracondylar Humerus Fractures.
articles.authors: Johnson QJ, Varas-Rodriguez E, Sullivan MH, Wahlig BD, Broida SE, Stans A, et al.
articles.population: Children who underwent surgical treatment for supracondylar humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Time to operating room following emergency department presentation; predictors of surgical delay beyond 18 hours
articles.take_home: Only 16% of children experienced surgical delay beyond 18 hours, with average time to surgery being 12.2 hours. Evening arrival at hospital and more severe fractures were the main factors associated with longer delays, which appear to be driven by system factors rather than clinical urgency.

articles.title: The rate of total hip arthroplasty after closed reduction of late-detected hip dislocation : 147 hips followed to patient age 70 years.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with registry follow-up
articles.population: Patients diagnosed with late-detected hip dislocation before age 3 years who underwent closed reduction without acetabular surgery
articles.outcomes: Rate of total hip arthroplasty (hip replacement) by patient age 70 years; risk factors for hip replacement; survival rates of hips without replacement
articles.take_home: Children with late-detected dislocated hips that were successfully reduced without additional surgery had good long-term outcomes if there was no remaining hip socket malformation, with only 24% needing hip replacement by age 70. However, those with remaining socket abnormalities had much worse outcomes, with 59% requiring hip replacement by age 70.

articles.title: From bowing to fracture : radiolucent lines as a predictor of progression in congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia.
articles.authors: Zhang S, Wang T, Zeng L, Xiao B, Mei H, Mao X, et al.
articles.population: Children with congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (Crawford types I to III)
articles.outcomes: Radiolucent lines as a predictor of fracture; fracture-free survival; independent risk factors for fracture identified by multivariable logistic regression
articles.take_home: Radiolucent lines on X-rays are a strong predictor of fracture in children with congenital bowing of the tibia, and combining this finding with the Crawford classification could help doctors decide which children need closer monitoring or earlier treatment.

articles.title: Evaluation of the clicky hip as a screening tool in the diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip.
articles.authors: Poacher AT, Bilal M, Smith A, Scourfield L, Hawes E, Ross M, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected registry data
articles.population: Live births in a UK tertiary centre catchment area undergoing newborn and six to eight week examinations
articles.sample_size: 42,338 infants analysed; 1,125 with documented clicky hip
articles.outcomes: Pathological developmental dysplasia of the hip requiring treatment; positive predictive value of clicky hip; number needed to screen
articles.take_home: A clicky hip found at newborn or six to eight week examination was associated with an increased risk of developmental dysplasia of the hip requiring treatment, though only about 3.6% of infants with a clicky hip actually had this condition. The findings support referring infants with a documented clicky hip for ultrasound screening.

articles.title: Femoral Nerve Palsy as a Complication of Pavlik Harness Treatment for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: Ten-Year Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Khan T, Douglas C, Khan Z, Edel P
articles.population: Infants with developmental dysplasia of the hip (Graf II to IV) treated with Pavlik harness
articles.sample_size: 339 infants, of which 20 developed femoral nerve palsy
articles.outcomes: Incidence of femoral nerve palsy, risk factors, recovery, and treatment success rates
articles.take_home: Femoral nerve palsy occurred in about 6% of infants treated with a Pavlik harness for hip dysplasia, but all cases recovered fully with harness adjustment. Although nerve palsy made treatment failure more common (35% vs 7%), it was not the main cause of failure; severe hip dysplasia was the key factor.
